title.en: Adjective + to-infinitive, and verbs of perception
title.es: Adjetivo + to-infinitive y verbos de percepción

summary.en: Many adjectives are followed by a **to-infinitive**: _glad **to see**_, _easy **to use**_, _likely **to happen**_. Some adjectives change pattern with the meaning: _afraid **to** do_ (too scared to act) and _afraid **of** doing_ (scared of the result). After **see, hear, watch, notice and feel**, use the **bare infinitive** for a complete action (_I saw him leave_) and the **-ing form** for an action in progress (_I saw him leaving_).
summary.es: Tras _see, hear, watch_ + persona no se usa **to**: _I saw him **leave**_ (acción completa) o _I saw him **leaving**_ (en curso). Y con adjetivos fáciles o difíciles se dice _difficult **to do**_, sin pronombre al final.

form: Adjective + **to-infinitive**: _pleased to hear_, _easy to use_, _certain to win_, _the first to arrive_
**It's** + adjective + (**for/of** someone) + **to-infinitive**: _It's essential for you to attend. It was kind of you to wait._
**afraid to** do (reluctant) / **afraid of** doing (fear of something happening)
**sorry to** hear or say (a reaction) / **sorry for / about** + noun or -ing (an apology)
**see, hear, watch, notice, feel** + object + **bare infinitive** (whole action) or **-ing** (action in progress)

uses.text: **Reaction or feeling**: _I was delighted **to hear** your news. She was surprised **to see** so many people._
**How easy, hard or safe something is**: _This app is easy **to use**. The water isn't safe **to drink**._

note.en: Do not repeat the object after the infinitive: _easy to use_, not _easy to use it_.
note.es: No repetimos el objeto al final: _easy to use_, no _easy to use it_.

uses.text: **Judging someone's behaviour** with **of**: _It was generous **of** you to lend me the money._ With **for**, we talk about the task: _It's important **for** staff to arrive early._
**Afraid**: _He was afraid **to tell** his boss_ (he did not tell him). _He was afraid **of losing** his job_ (the thing he feared).
**Perception verbs**: _I heard her **sing**_ (the whole song). _I heard her **singing** in the shower_ (the action was going on). Not _I heard her to sing_.

mistakes.wrong: I saw him to leave the building.
mistakes.right: I saw him leave the building.

why.en: After see, hear and watch with an object, we use the bare infinitive or -ing, never to.
why.es: Después de _see / hear / watch_ + objeto no se usa **to**.

mistakes.wrong: This exercise is difficult to do it.
mistakes.right: This exercise is difficult to do.

why.en: The subject of the sentence is already the object of the infinitive, so we do not add it.
why.es: En español decimos «es difícil de hacerlo», pero en inglés no se repite el objeto.

mistakes.wrong: It was kind from you to help us.
mistakes.right: It was kind of you to help us.

why.en: To judge someone's behaviour we say kind of you, not from you.
why.es: «Qué amable por tu parte» es _kind **of** you_.

mistakes.wrong: I was glad of see them all together.
mistakes.right: I was glad to see them all together.

why.en: After glad we use a to-infinitive to give the reason for the feeling.
why.es: Tras _glad / pleased / happy_ que expresan la reacción se usa **to** + infinitivo.

examples.en: I'm delighted to hear that you've passed.
examples.es: Me alegra saber que has aprobado.

examples.en: This printer is really easy to use.
It's essential for all staff to attend the briefing.
It was kind of you to lend me your charger.
examples.es: Fue muy amable por tu parte dejarme el cargador.

examples.en: She was the first to arrive and the last to leave.
He was afraid to ask for a pay rise, so he never mentioned it.
He was afraid of losing his job, so he worked late every night.
I was sorry to hear about your accident.
I saw him leave the building at six.
examples.es: Lo vi salir del edificio a las seis.

examples.en: We watched the sun going down behind the hills.
She heard the neighbours arguing through the wall.

practice.prompt: I was surprised ___ so many people at the meeting.

explanation.en: Surprised is followed by a to-infinitive when it names the reaction.

practice.prompt: This new software is very easy ___.

explanation.en: Easy takes a to-infinitive, with no pronoun after it.

practice.prompt: I noticed a man ___ photos of the building for twenty minutes.

explanation.en: The action lasted for some time and was in progress, so we use -ing. After notice we never use to.

practice.prompt: She didn't go out alone because she was afraid of ___ lost.

explanation.en: Afraid of is followed by an -ing form.

practice.prompt: It was very generous ___ you to pay for everyone.

explanation.en: We judge a person's behaviour with generous of you.
